title: Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations
main_claim: For every invertible mixing probability-preserving T on an arbitrary probability space and bounded f1,f2,f3, (1/N)Σ f1(T^n x)f2(T^{2n}x)f3(T^{3n}x) → Π∫f_j a.e. The proof goes through an oscillation inequality for smooth dyadic averages (Prop 2.2), which is deduced from a depth-varying local-form estimate (Thm 3.2). That estimate is an extension of the companion paper H (L^3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform).

issues.location: Sections 5–7 (base.tex, localization.tex, completion.tex): proof of Theorem thm:depth-local
issues.description: The depth-varying local estimate, which is the whole analytic core, is proved by adapting the internal steps of companion paper H. Typical phrasing is 'run H's Section 10 construction with these substitutions'. The cited H equations (\Heq{19}, short-block comparison, packing of attempts, order of parameters) and H's parameter-order requirement C19^H C5^H (q-2)<1/8 are invoked but not restated. So the result is conditional on H, and on the claim that H's proof goes through with the substitutions. This cannot be checked from this paper alone. I found no specific failing step.
issues.evidence: completion.tex: 'This is the conditional retained-cell calculation of [H, Section 10], with its basic square, variation, and frozen-row hypotheses supplied above'; also 'its proof permits the choice required here' for the common q. H itself was audited by family 086 with partial coverage (localization internals only skimmed).

issues.location: ergodic.tex, proof of Theorem 1.1 vs Proposition prop:orbit-oscillation
issues.description: Plausibility flag, not a demonstrated error. The oscillation inequality (Prop 2.2) is claimed for every invertible system. Mixing is used only to identify the limit through norm convergence. Host–Kra norm convergence would serve the same purpose for any system, and the rational-grid argument is system-free. So the paper's machinery, if correct, would prove pointwise convergence of the n,2n,3n averages on every invertible system. The paper itself cites that problem as open (KMPWW 2026, Sec 1.8 item 5). This much stronger hidden consequence calls for extra scrutiny of the H-based Theorem 3.2.
issues.evidence: Lemma ergodic-cauchy and Prop orbit-oscillation give a.e. convergence of V_k^φ on every system. The identification step uses only ||V_k^φ − L||_2 → 0, and the grid step uses only |A_N| ≤ 1.

- rows.tex: input size/variation lemma; private catalog bounds; maximal row lemma (whole-row bucket assignment via the refinement chain, many-hit bound, prefix domination, binary-prefix L² bound, weak-to-L¹ integration giving 2H|R|^{1/2}); depth-varying row lemma (Abel summation sign checked, Cauchy–Schwarz over W blocks); projection-increment corollary.
- Skimmed only: base.tex, localization.tex and completion.tex, i.e. the adaptation of H's internals, including the short-block fixed-input comparison and the choice of q / absorption.
